Grade segments by expected use, 0 to 1

Source: R/grade.R
knw_grade.Rd

A segment's grade is the curve's predicted detection rate at the segment's size, gradient and distance to a river, at the reference nuisance values and with the group random effect excluded (so grades compare across groups), divided by the ref_quantile of that rate over the species' accessible segments (those of them ref_rows marks), and capped at 1. The top of the reference segments reads 1, and a segment at a third of that rate reads about 0.3. It is expected use per standard electrofishing visit, not habitat quality, and is labelled so.

Usage

knw_grade(
  curve,
  segments,
  cols = c(size = "mad_pick", grad = "gradient", dist = "dist_m"),
  ref_quantile = 0.95,
  classes = c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1),
  ref_rows = NULL
)

Arguments

curve

the list knw_tune_curve() returns.

segments

data.frame with accessible (logical) and the columns cols name: the size variable the curve was fit on, the gradient, and dist_m (metres to the first river of the curve's q; NA or Inf where none).

cols

named character: size, grad, dist.

ref_quantile

numeric(1) the quantile of the reference segments' rate (accessible, and marked by ref_rows) that reads 1.

classes

numeric the class breaks on the grade.

ref_rows

NULL, or a logical vector of nrow(segments) marking the segments the reference is taken over (among the accessible ones), such as the stream branch the curve was fitted on. NULL takes every accessible segment. Every segment is graded either way.

Value

A list: grades, a tibble of nrow(segments) with rate, grade, grade_class; reference, the rate that reads 1; dropped, counts of segments with no size or gradient.

Details

A segment whose size variable is missing (an unmeasured first-order stream under a width model; a segment with no flow even from a parent under a MAD model) or whose gradient is missing gets NA, and the counts come back. A missing distance is the cap (dist_cap_m): the walk found no river of at least the curve's q downstream (the sea came first, or the walk stopped), not that the segment is far from any river. knw_grade_species() walks every gradable accessible segment, so a segment reads the cap only for that reason.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
g <- knw_grade(cv, seg, cols = c(size = "mad_pick", grad = "gradient", dist = "dist_m"))
table(g$grades$grade_class, useNA = "ifany")
} # }
